clue.text: A manic GP plans for battle

indicators.note: to plan is to arrange or work out, so these letters are to be arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A deranged family doctor draws up strategy for a war.
explanation.definitionFit: A military operation or series of engagements in a war is a campaign, so a battle stands for it.

clue.text: All countries come to terms with worry

parts.note: UN, the United Nations, takes in nearly all the world's countries
to settle is to reach an agreement, to come to terms

explanation.surface: Every nation has to learn to live with anxiety.
explanation.definitionFit: To worry someone is to disturb or upset their composure, a near synonym.

clue.text: A front row forward (very large) would be appropriate

parts.note: in rugby the props are forwards in the front row of the scrum
OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize

explanation.surface: A huge rugby forward would be just the right choice for the team.
explanation.walkthrough: A prop is a front-row forward in rugby union or league; OS (outsize) is a size label on clothes in British shops.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pertinent or fitting to the matter in hand is said to be apropos of it, a synonym of appropriate.

clue.text: Sudden attack on mint

explanation.surface: A surprise raid is launched on the Royal Mint.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden military attack is an air or ground strike, and to mint coins is to stamp or strike them from metal.

clue.text: Soap from Israel, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests a possible variant form, so the letters of the country's name are rearranged

explanation.surface: A television drama imported from the Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: A soap opera is a broadcast drama told in instalments, a continuing story.

clue.text: Anoraks with platform shoes?

parts.note: anoraks are obsessive hobbyists, and these ones are shod for standing on railway platforms noting engine numbers, not wearing tall seventies footwear

explanation.surface: Geeks dressed in raincoats and towering heels.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang an anorak is an obsessive, socially awkward enthusiast, after the hooded jackets worn by people logging train numbers at stations.
explanation.definitionFit: Rail enthusiasts who record locomotive numbers are the classic example of the British slang term anoraks.

clue.text: Calls to account?

parts.note: call to account usually means hold someone responsible, but here it is the phone calls set out on a statement of charges

explanation.surface: Someone is being held responsible for their actions.
explanation.definitionFit: A statement from the phone company lists the calls made and the money owed for them.

clue.text: Purchases that add spice to journeys?

definitions.text: Purchases that add spice to journeys?

parts.words: Purchases that add spice to journeys?
parts.note: season can mean add spice to food, and tickets are what admit you to journeys, so a whimsical reading of a commuter's long-term travel pass

explanation.surface: Buying things that make a trip more exciting.
explanation.walkthrough: To season food is to spice it; a season ticket is a pass bought for a long period of regular travel or admission.
explanation.definitionFit: A commuter pays upfront for months of travel by buying passes valid over a long period.

clue.text: Electronic circuits need energy to run by

parts.note: E is a common abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail
laps are circuits of a racetrack
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Electronic wiring requires power before it can operate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Electronic circuits' reads as wiring, but the circuits are laps of a track.
explanation.definitionFit: When time passes or slips away, it is said to run by.

clue.text: Love a girl in novel?

annotationWithheld.why: Love a girl in novel? (8): O + anagram of A GIRL IN gives the letters, but 'novel' must be both the anagram indicator and the definition, one word doing two jobs

clue.text: A hint of asparagus

parts.note: a hint suggests a faint taste, but the clue also points to the pointed edible end of an asparagus spear, and a hint is also a useful pointer

explanation.definitionFit: A helpful hint is a pointer, and the edible pointed end of an asparagus spear has the same name.

clue.text: Ruined Italian banker covered by deposit

indicators.note: covered by means the river is enclosed within the deposit word, wrapped on both sides

parts.note: silt is fine sediment deposited by flowing water
the Po is Italy's longest river; a river is a banker because it has banks

explanation.surface: An Italian financier is ruined after being buried in debts and deposits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banker' is crossword code for a river, which has banks; here it is the Po, Italy's longest.
explanation.definitionFit: Something damaged or wrecked beyond use is said to be spoiled or spoilt.

clue.text: Have a view on past appearance

parts.note: over means finished, gone by, as in the party is over
someone's look is their appearance

explanation.surface: Having an opinion on someone's earlier style.
explanation.definitionFit: A house that has a view of the sea looks down upon it from above, a synonym.

clue.text: Legendary flier from the Catholic church embraces love

indicators.note: embraces means the church abbreviation holds the letter for love within its arms

parts.note: RC stands for Roman Catholic
love is nil in tennis scoring, written as O

explanation.surface: A mythical winged being emerges from Rome's church, full of love.
explanation.walkthrough: The roc is a giant bird of Arabian legend, in the tales of Sinbad.
explanation.definitionFit: A monstrous bird from Middle Eastern myth, strong enough to carry off elephants.

clue.text: Dogged dog chased Charles out

parts.note: a hound is a hunting dog

indicators.note: out means the short form of the name is taken away from the word chased

parts.note: Chas is the usual short form of the name Charles

explanation.surface: A determined dog pursued a man named Charles away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes CHAS (short for Charles) from CHASED, leaving ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Being dogged means being followed or harassed persistently, as by a pursuing pack.

clue.text: Understand that sources of diamonds interest girls

indicators.note: the sources of words are their beginnings, so take each word's opening letter

explanation.surface: Grasp the fact that the origins of diamonds fascinate young women.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for understand or appreciate, as in 'I can see what you mean, man'.

clue.text: Brogues for a dollar?

parts.note: a dollar is a hundred cents, and C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, giving C plus cents

explanation.surface: Buying sturdy leather shoes for just one dollar?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brogues' looks like shoes, but a brogue is a regional, especially Irish, way of speaking. A dollar is 'a C cents', a hundred cents.
explanation.definitionFit: A brogue is a regional lilt of speech, especially Irish, so brogues are ways of pronouncing.

clue.text: Prisoners welcoming excursion to form lines

indicators.note: welcoming means the inmates' word takes the trip word in, inside itself

parts.note: cons is short for convicts, prisoners
a tour is an excursion or trip

explanation.surface: Inmates greet a visiting party and line up.
explanation.definitionFit: On a map, curves joining points of equal height are lines of equal elevation.

clue.text: Arouse hostility and set off to the mountains

indicators.note: off suggests something gone wrong or out of order, so the little word is jumbled

parts.note: a range is a chain of mountains

explanation.surface: A quarrel breaks out and someone heads for the hills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set off' reads as departing for the hills, but 'off' is the anagram signal working on 'set' alone, giving EST.
explanation.definitionFit: To alienate people is to turn them unfriendly towards each other.

clue.text: To remonstrate or demonstrate one more time

parts.note: re- is a prefix meaning again
to prove something is to demonstrate it

explanation.surface: Should one protest or show the case again?
explanation.definitionFit: To rebuke or scold someone is to remonstrate with them about their conduct.

clue.text: Breeding exercises require sound university qualification

parts.note: PE stands for physical education, school exercises

indicators.note: sound tells us the word for an academic award is heard, not seen, and spelt as it is spoken

parts.note: a degree is a qualification awarded by a university

explanation.surface: Workouts are needed to earn a graduate diploma in animal husbandry.
explanation.walkthrough: The second syllable of the award word is heard as 'di-gree', and that spoken form is what is written.
explanation.definitionFit: Good breeding means distinguished ancestry, a recorded line of descent.

clue.text: Relatives at home with regulations

parts.note: staying in means being at home
statutes or rules passed by parliament

explanation.surface: Family members sit by the fire with the rule book.
explanation.definitionFit: Relatives by marriage, such as a spouse's parents, are a kind of relation.

clue.text: Make copies and exit at speed

explanation.surface: Print some duplicates, then dash out of the door.
explanation.definitionFit: To print or photocopy a batch is to produce copies quickly, and to flee is to bolt hastily away.

clue.text: Leaving work?

parts.note: read as going home at the end of the day, but it means the formal warning an employee gives before quitting a job

explanation.definitionFit: An employee resigning must hand in a formal warning of departure to the employer.

clue.text: Trophy for best to reverse

indicators.note: to reverse means the word for best is to be written back to front

parts.note: top means best, as in top marks

explanation.surface: A cup awarded to whoever performs the finest reversing manoeuvre.
explanation.definitionFit: A silver cup won in a contest is informally called this, from the shape.

clue.text: Crown Derby manufacturer?

parts.note: Crown Derby suggests fine English porcelain, but a crown is the top of a hat and a derby is a bowler hat, so this is a hat-maker

explanation.surface: Who makes the famous English porcelain?
explanation.walkthrough: Royal Crown Derby is a famous English porcelain; a derby is a bowler hat and the crown is a hat's top.
explanation.definitionFit: A hat-maker shapes crowns of hats such as the derby, the American bowler.

clue.text: Spoke at length — nothing highly thought of

parts.note: O is the round figure zero, nothing
rated means held in high regard, as in a highly rated player

explanation.surface: Someone talks for ages but nobody thinks much of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who delivered a long formal speech held forth or declaimed.

clue.text: Means test legislation?

parts.note: a means test checks benefit claimants' income, but read means as averages, as in statistics, and the principle governing them

explanation.surface: A bill to assess people's income before giving benefit.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a means test checks a person's income before state benefit is given; here means are statistical averages.
explanation.definitionFit: The supposed principle that chance events even out over time is a rule about statistical means.
